Hi Sara / Rivermind ops team,

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. Per our convo, I pulled together the first-pass sizing questions and a short checklist so we can lock down networking boundaries and throughput targets before our on-site kickoff. Attached: rivermind_workload_trace.csv (sample 7-day traces) and network_diagram_v2.png.

High-level asks for alignment:
- Confirm target SLOs: 99th token latency <= 180ms, P95 tail <= 120ms for interactive assistants.
- Steady-state throughput target: 150 inference requests/sec (avg request = 120 tokens).
- Burst target: 450 req/sec for 5 minute sustained windows (30 minute hourly peaks).
- Desired headroom: pref 30% (autoscale buffer + warm pool).
- Allowed egress/peering: what egress rates can your VPC sustain to our control plane? Any proxy appliances in path?
- Networking: do you require private peering only, or will an internet-based TLS tunnel (mutual TLS) be used for model telemetry/metrics?

Operational constraints we need to finalize:
- Encryption/KMS: any HSM/KMS constraints for model keys or request metadata?
- Audit retention: required retention windows for request logs (30/90/365 days?).

Next steps: if you can confirm the two bullets above (SLOs + throughput targets) and upload the synthetic peak traces (or confirm the attached sample is representative), we’ll produce a 2-page sizing note in 48 hours with recommended GPU counts, warm-pool strategy, and a networking fencepost proposal.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Jonas for the sizing calc once you confirm.

Laura — thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers and an attachment of our internal peak summary (rivermind_peaks.json).

- SLOs: the 99th <=180ms target is fine; P95 at 120ms is our internal goal for interactive features. For non-interactive batched jobs (report generation) we can tolerate higher latency.
- Throughput: the attached traces show our current app-level peaks ~380 req/sec (90th percentile peaks), sustained traffic is ~120 req/sec. The big delta is that some campaigns will produce heavy 10–15 min spikes up to ~520 req/sec — we included those in the peaks file.
- Egress/peering: we can do private peering (Direct Connect) or a dedicated transit peer; egress capacity from our VPC is limited to 10 Gbps for the first phase (we can expand). No inline proxies that rewrite headers, but we do force TLS mTLS at our edge.
- KMS: we use a hosted KMS (AWS KMS), can support envelope encryption; no in-house HSM for keys.
- Audit retention: default 90 days, 365 days available under the enterprise addendum.

Questions for you:
1) If we need 30% headroom for bursts to 520 req/sec, what does that imply for GPU counts assuming model mix (13B + 70B occasional)?
2) Do you recommend colocating model caches on the same rack to reduce egress?

Thanks — cc'ing ops so they see the attachment.

—Sara

Sara / Laura — I ran a first-order sizing with the numbers you sent. Below is a conservative, operationally realistic recommendation (we'll formalize in the 2-page note):

Assumptions (from your traces + typical model perf):
- Typical request: 120 tokens (prompt+response).
- Model mix: 75% 13B-class (quantized), 25% 70B-class (FP16/quant).
- Target SLO: P95 <=120ms interactive, 99th token <=180ms.
- Warm pool buffer goal: 30% (to absorb short spikes).

Sizing (ballpark):
- Baseline sustained capacity: 150 req/sec => ~18M tokens/sec (150 * 120).
- Burst capacity target: 520 req/sec => ~62.4M tokens/sec.
- Effective tokens/s per GPU (conservative):
  - H100 (FP16, large seq): ~6M tokens/s (real-world numbers vary; we use conservative 6M for 70B workload).
  - A30/A10G (quantized 13B): ~3.2M tokens/s per card for 13B quantized workloads.

Recommended configuration (phase 1):
- Mix: 6 x H100 + 20 x A10G equivalent (or 12 x H100 + 10 x A10G depending on cost & locality).
  - Rationale: H100s carry the 70B tail; A10Gs handle the bulk of the 13B throughput efficiently when quantized.
- Warm pool: keep ~25% of GPUs pre-warmed (for example 7 GPUs reserved in the pool) to hit 30% headroom for sub-minute spikes.
- Autoscale: admission control that prioritizes requests by SLA class — interactive assistant > scheduled batches. Burst policies: prefer horizontal scale on A10G pool first, then H100 fallthrough.
- Networking: 10 Gbps egress will be a hard cap for the first phase; with 10 Gbps you should plan traffic shaping & batching for telemetry. We recommend colocating model cache + KV store in the same rack (or same VPC private subnet) to avoid cross-rack egress for KV hits.

Latency & batching guidance:
- Use small dynamic batching (batch windows <= 20ms) for interactive; larger batching for scheduled jobs.
- Enable KV cache for frequent prefixes & maintain a small local LRU cache per GPU to reduce repeat token computation.

Open decisions for us to finalize:
- Exact GPU SKUs (we can run cost/throughput sims for H100 vs H200 if you plan to purchase).
- Warm-pool sizing policy: fixed reserved vs progressive reserved based on time-of-day.
- Networking topology: private peering topology and expected MTU for large payloads — any limit on jumbo frames?

I'll produce the 2-page sizing note + a simple spreadsheet (privpool_initial_sizing_spreadsheet.xlsx) by EOD that enumerates tradeoffs (cost vs latency vs headroom). Laura — want me to send that to the HubSpot ticket or directly to Rivermind?

Jonas
